question: Do shallow vision-network layers transiently acquire representations that are robust to natural corruptions early in ordinary training, and can freezing or rewinding those layers preserve that robustness without changing the architecture?

key_findings.claim: Standard corruption-robust training recipes primarily repair deep representations while leaving a shallow-subnetwork robustness gap.
key_findings.evidence: Layerwise linear probes on ResNet-50 show that AugMix, Mixup, and an improved torchvision recipe reduce the clean-corrupted performance gap mainly at deep subnetworks such as layers 40 and 49, with shallow probes near layers 1 and 10 remaining close to the plain baseline.

key_findings.claim: Shallow clean-versus-corrupted feature agreement peaks early and fades as clean-data optimization continues.
key_findings.evidence: For a ResNet-18 training trajectory, consecutive shallow weights remain directionally active early rather than immediately converging. Centered Kernel Alignment between clean and corrupted features declines progressively in the stem and Stage 1, increasingly at corruption severities 3-5; InfoNCE-based mutual-information estimates show a parallel loss of information preservation in shallow layers while Stage 4 is comparatively stagnant.

key_findings.claim: Freezing an early shallow checkpoint changes the geometry reached by later layers, supporting a causal role for the early configuration within the tested protocol.
key_findings.evidence: The authors freeze shallow subnetworks taken at early, intermediate, or late epochs and retrain the remaining layers. Early anchors lead to visibly smoother corruption-perturbed loss surfaces and lower local sharpness than later anchors, even after the deep network is reoptimized.

key_findings.claim: Two minimal trajectory interventions preserve or recover the proposed early robust state.
key_findings.evidence: Early-Phase Stabilization freezes the shallow parameters after an intervention epoch while deep parameters continue training. Asymmetric Weight Reversion saves a shallow checkpoint, restores it at a later epoch, reduces its subsequent learning rate, and lets the deep subnetwork realign. Neither method adds a learnable module, although both introduce scheduling choices.

key_findings.claim: EPS and AWR improve ImageNet-C accuracy over the paper's 90-epoch ResNet-50 baseline, and can add gains to stronger augmentations.
key_findings.evidence: On ImageNet-C, the baseline reaches 39.2% top-1 accuracy, EPS 42.5%, AWR 43.1%, and AWR combined with the improved recipe 46.5%. The plain AWR gain is 3.9 percentage points and the combined gain is 7.3 points over the plain baseline; the table also reports SAM at 39.8%, DAMP at 41.4%, and DAT at 41.1%.

key_findings.claim: The intervention usually reduces average corruption error across heterogeneous backbones and remains complementary to common training regularizers.
key_findings.evidence: On ImageNet-100 variants, EPS or AWR improves average mCE for MobileNetV2, WideResNet-50, MobileViT-S, EfficientFormer-L1, and MambaOut-femto, with reported reductions ranging from 0.5 to 4.7 for EPS and up to 11.5 for AWR in the displayed configurations. When combined with AugMix, AutoAugment, CutMix, label smoothing, or dropout on ImageNet-1K, the interventions reduce average mCE by up to 1.9 beyond the paired recipe.

key_findings.claim: Robust shallow pretraining transfers beyond classification, but several gains are modest and come with clean-task tradeoffs.
key_findings.evidence: On COCO-C, the intervention raises Faster R-CNN mAP from 17.5 to 17.9 and YOLOv5 from 19.9 to 24.3, while clean mAP falls from 37.6 to 37.0 and 39.8 to 37.9. Corrupted Cityscapes mIoU rises by 3.7 for DeepLabV3+ and 3.1 for GCNet; average ACDC gains are only 0.1 and 0.7 mIoU and some rain results worsen.

key_findings.claim: EPS/AWR initialization improves several continual online test-time adaptation methods under severe ImageNet-C shift.
key_findings.evidence: At severity 5, EPS or AWR increases top-1 accuracy for RoTTA, AdaContrast, Tent, SAR, and RMT. The largest displayed changes include AdaContrast from 34.9% to 37.5% with AWR, RoTTA from 32.6% to 34.4% with EPS, and RMT from 42.2% to 43.8% with EPS.

key_findings.claim: Post hoc geometry, dimensionality, shape, and frequency probes are consistent with the preservation story, but do not uniquely identify its mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Relative to baseline, EPS and AWR suppress local sharpness growth and input-gradient norms, reduce clean-corrupted changes in effective rank and intrinsic dimension, produce more compact t-SNE clusters, retain more accuracy after patch shuffling, and reduce mid-to-high-frequency error. These are mutually consistent correlates measured after intervention rather than independent causal tests of a single pathway.

method.core_idea: Treat common-corruption robustness as a transient property of the optimization trajectory: diagnose when shallow clean/corrupted representations are most stable, then constrain only those shallow weights while allowing deeper semantic layers to finish fitting.
method.mechanism: Split network parameters into shallow and deep subnetworks. Track shallow weight-direction changes, clean-corrupted CKA, InfoNCE mutual-information estimates, and perturbed loss surfaces across checkpoints. For EPS, stop all shallow updates at epoch tau while continuing ordinary deep-layer SGD. For AWR, save a shallow snapshot at an earlier epoch, restore it at a later intervention epoch, and continue shallow training with a much smaller learning rate while leaving the deep learning rate unchanged. Pretrain backbones on clean ImageNet, reserve corrupted datasets for inference, and test classification corruption accuracy, mCE, dense-prediction transfer, online adaptation, physical adverse conditions, timing sensitivity, and geometry correlates.
assumptions: High clean-corrupted CKA and an InfoNCE mutual-information estimate in shallow layers reflect task-useful robustness rather than generic underfitting.
A flatter loss surface under selected input perturbations predicts robustness to the benchmark's natural corruptions.
The chosen shallow/deep boundary has comparable functional meaning across CNN, vision-transformer, and Mamba-style backbones.
Freezing or lowering the shallow learning rate preserves useful low-level structure while deeper layers retain enough capacity to recover clean-task fit.
Corruption benchmark improvements transfer to real deployment shifts even though most evaluation corruptions are synthetic.
Intervention epochs and the AWR post-reversion learning rate can be selected without leaking information from the corruption test sets.
The reported robust state is a property of training dynamics rather than a specific recipe, random seed, or checkpoint-selection artifact.

techniques.role: Measures where robustness gaps live by fitting linear probes to progressively deeper subnetworks.
Locates the early period in which shallow parameter directions are still being actively reorganized.
Tracks structural agreement between representations of clean and naturally corrupted versions of the same inputs.
Uses a contrastive lower-bound estimator as a second view of corruption-conditioned information retention.
Holds shallow states from different epochs fixed while reoptimizing deep layers to test their effect on the attainable landscape.
Truncates the shallow optimization trajectory at an early epoch while deep training continues.
Restores only shallow weights to a historical state and reduces their subsequent update intensity.
Connects robustness changes to local sharpness, gradient flatness, effective rank, intrinsic dimension, shape dependence, and frequency error.

evaluations.setting: Randomly initialized ResNet-50 trained on ImageNet for 90 epochs, tested on ImageNet-C
evaluations.result: EPS 42.5%, AWR 43.1%, and AWR with improved recipe 46.5%
evaluations.baseline: Plain baseline 39.2%; representative alternatives include SAM 39.8%, DAMP 41.4%, and DAT 41.1%

evaluations.setting: Five CNN, hybrid, transformer, and Mamba-style backbones on ImageNet-100-C, ImageNet-100-bar-C, ImageNet-100-3DCC, and ImageNet-100V2-C
evaluations.metric: Clean top-1 accuracy and average mCE
evaluations.result: EPS/AWR reduce average mCE across every displayed backbone-condition pairing, by 0.5 to 11.5 points depending on recipe and architecture
evaluations.baseline: Each backbone's matched training recipe without the trajectory intervention

evaluations.setting: ImageNet-1K training with AugMix, AutoAugment, CutMix, label smoothing, or dropout
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy and average mCE over four corruption suites
evaluations.result: EPS or AWR adds up to a 1.9-point average-mCE reduction beyond the paired augmentation or regularizer
evaluations.baseline: The same strong augmentation or regularization recipe alone

evaluations.setting: COCO-C detection with Faster R-CNN and YOLOv5
evaluations.result: Corrupted mAP gains are +0.4 and +4.4, while clean mAP changes are -0.6 and -1.9

evaluations.setting: ADE20K-C and Cityscapes-C semantic segmentation with DeepLabV3+ and GCNet
evaluations.result: Corrupted gains range from +0.7 to +3.7; several clean scores decrease by 0.3-1.3

evaluations.setting: Continual online test-time adaptation on ImageNet-C severity 5
evaluations.result: Positive gains for all five displayed adapters, up to +2.6 for AdaContrast with AWR
evaluations.baseline: RoTTA, AdaContrast, Tent, SAR, or RMT initialized from the ordinary backbone

evaluations.result: Average gains are +0.1 for DeepLabV3+ and +0.7 for GCNet, with a tradeoff on rain
evaluations.baseline: The same segmentation architectures without intervention

evaluations.setting: Intervention timing, reversion anchor, trigger epoch, and shallow learning-rate sweeps on ImageNet-100 corruption suites
evaluations.result: EPS remains above baseline for intervention epochs 0-40; AWR is robust over early anchors 0-30 and shallow learning rates 1e-6 to 1e-3, but degrades when triggered after roughly epoch 35 or at learning rate 1e-1
evaluations.baseline: Unintervened model and the default EPS/AWR settings

limitations: Author-stated: preserving early shallow priors is aimed at low-level visual corruption and is not a complete solution to semantic, contextual, or sensor-domain distribution shift.

Reviewer-identified: the paper reports point estimates without seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests for the main benchmark tables, leaving robustness to initialization and data order unclear.

Reviewer-identified: EPS and AWR are called parameter-free only in the sense of adding no learnable weights; they still require a shallow/deep boundary, intervention epoch, snapshot epoch, trigger epoch, and AWR shallow learning rate.

Reviewer-identified: the test corruptions are said to be inference-only, but the paper does not give a fully independent clean-data rule for selecting all intervention hyperparameters, so corruption-suite tuning leakage is difficult to rule out.

Reviewer-identified: freezing experiments isolate checkpoint timing imperfectly because deeper weights are retrained under a new constrained optimization problem; flatter surfaces and robust accuracy remain associated rather than mechanistically identified.

Reviewer-identified: CKA and InfoNCE estimates are shown mostly as curves without numeric effect sizes, estimator uncertainty, or controls for the possibility that early shallow layers are simply less specialized.
Reviewer-identified: several downstream gains are small, some corruptions worsen, and clean detection or segmentation performance often declines.

Reviewer-identified: the baseline is a 90-epoch ResNet recipe without modern augmentation; stronger-recipe combinations help, but not every headline comparison is compute- and recipe-matched to current robust training.

Reviewer-identified: the exact definition of the shallow subnetwork and its translation across architectures is under-specified in the main text, limiting reproducibility and the architecture-agnostic claim.
Reviewer-identified: no adversarial, calibration, certified, or worst-group robustness evaluation establishes whether the intervention generalizes beyond common-corruption accuracy.
failure_modes: Freezing too early preserves generic low-frequency features but blocks task-relevant adaptation, reducing clean accuracy.
Freezing too late captures the already sharpened shallow state and provides little robustness benefit.
AWR uses a post-reversion shallow learning rate that is too high, quickly erasing the restored state; at 1e-1 the reported optimization becomes unstable.
Reverting shallow weights creates a feature-interface mismatch that deep layers cannot repair within the remaining schedule.
A corruption depends on high-level semantics rather than low-level texture or frequency, so shallow stabilization is irrelevant or harmful.
An architecture lacks a clean stem/stage split, making the shallow intervention boundary arbitrary.
Benchmark selection favors the same corruption statistics used to identify the early checkpoint, inflating apparent generality.
The method improves mean corruption accuracy while sacrificing a safety-critical condition, as some rain and clean-task results illustrate.
reusable_insights: Treat checkpoint time and network depth as separate axes when diagnosing robustness; endpoint probes can miss transient useful states.
Freeze-and-retrain from multiple layer checkpoints to test whether a representation changes the solutions available to the remaining network.
Preserve a useful early subnetwork while allowing later modules to realign, rather than early-stopping the entire model.
Report clean-task changes beside corruption gains because robustness interventions can move the operating frontier rather than dominate it.
Use multiple representation and geometry probes as converging evidence, but avoid treating correlated diagnostics as independent causal proof.
Define an intervention-selection rule on clean training or a held-out corruption development set before testing on benchmark corruptions.
Test trajectory interventions as initializations for downstream adaptation, where stable low-level features may reduce collapse.
open_questions: Does robustness fading replicate across many seeds under a pre-registered clean-only checkpoint-selection rule?
Which exact shallow filters or circuits disappear late, and can causal feature replacement identify them more directly than CKA?
Can intervention timing be predicted online from weight velocity or representation stability without access to corrupted validation data?
How should the shallow/deep boundary be selected for ViTs, state-space models, multimodal encoders, and dense prediction networks?
Can a soft regularizer preserve early robust directions without the clean-accuracy loss caused by hard freezing?
Does EPS/AWR improve adversarial, calibration, worst-group, and real sensor-shift robustness, or only average common-corruption accuracy?
Are the flatness and spectral changes causes of robustness or downstream consequences of reduced shallow plasticity?
What happens when the robust early state conflicts with a necessary domain-specific low-level adaptation during transfer?

competitive_landscape.title: Overfitting in Adversarially Robust Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Rice et al. establish robust overfitting over training time and show that whole-model early stopping is a powerful remedy, but in adversarial training under norm-bounded attacks. This paper targets ordinary clean training and natural corruptions, localizes fading to shallow representations, and preserves continued deep-layer fitting through partial freezing or rewinding.

competitive_landscape.title: The Early Phase of Neural Network Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Frankle et al. already demonstrate that important, non-independent structural changes and critical periods occur within the first training iterations. The present work narrows that temporal thesis to clean-to-common-corruption stability in shallow vision layers and converts it into two robustness interventions with cross-task evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Robustness by Enhancing Weak Subnets
competitive_landscape.difference: EWS directly links weak internal subnetworks to corruption vulnerability, searches for them, and strengthens them by distillation from the full model. EPS/AWR focus specifically on shallow subnetworks and their temporal state, avoid subnet search and teacher distillation, and intervene by stopping or reversing their trajectory.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamic Sparse Training versus Dense Training: The Unexpected Winner in Image Corruption Robustness
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. show that continuously evolving sparse connectivity can outperform dense training on image and video corruption robustness across architectures. This paper retains dense architecture and instead constrains when shallow weights may change, trading dynamic topology for checkpoint-state preservation and a different hypothesis about early low-level priors.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Robustness against Common Corruptions with Frequency Biased Models
competitive_landscape.difference: RoHL explicitly builds and ensembles high- and low-frequency experts and regularizes feature-map total variation to cover heterogeneous corruptions. EPS/AWR use no expert architecture or corruption-specific loss; their frequency-error improvements emerge after temporal shallow-layer intervention, but they do not match RoHL's explicit per-corruption specialization analysis.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the paper identifies previously overlooked natural-corruption 'robustness fading' in shallow layers and introduces the first parameter-free trajectory interventions that stabilize or recover the transient state across architectures and tasks. Early critical periods, robust overfitting, weak-subnetwork enhancement, robust lottery tickets, and frequency- or architecture-biased front ends all predate it. Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is the conjunction of a depth-by-time diagnosis with two extremely simple partial-training controls—freeze the shallow prefix early or rewind only that prefix and reduce its learning rate—plus broad common-corruption transfer tests. The evidence supports a useful empirical recipe and a plausible preservation hypothesis, but the term 'parameter-free' is imprecise, the mechanism is correlational beyond the constrained retraining study, and missing seed statistics and independent checkpoint-selection details weaken the strength of the general claim.
reviewer_notes: All 19 pages were checked, including the representation and freezing diagnostics, Algorithm 1, benchmark tables, timing sweeps, geometry probes, discussion boundary, and references. Clean-performance decreases and the small ACDC effects were retained rather than reporting only robust gains. Competitive identifiers and abstracts were verified on primary arXiv records current through 2026-08-23.
